title: Policy benchmark with measured clock sensitivity (M001: RTX 5070)
research_question: Do the Phase 1 conclusions survive when the two parameters measured on real hardware (clock sensitivity of compute-bound and memory-bound work) replace the placeholders?
hypothesis: Inherited from E001 and re-tested: H1: joint uses less energy per successful task than independent in at least 4 of 6 scenarios (paired 95% CI entirely below 0), without more SLO violations or thermal-limit exceedances. H2: every optimising policy uses less energy per successful task than fixed in every scenario. New: HC1: compute_only saves more energy per successful task relative to fixed in E001C than in E001, in all 6 scenarios (seed-paired change in relative saving, 95% CI entirely below 0), because with beta_memory = 0 memory-bound phases lose no throughput when the clock drops. HC2: that change is largest in S5_memory_heavy. HC3: joint's advantage over independent changes by less than 0.5 percentage points (95% CI of the seed-paired change within +/-0.5 pp) in at least 5 of 6 scenarios, because both policies use the same DVFS model.
null_hypothesis: Calibrating clock sensitivity changes neither the savings from DVFS nor the policy ranking.
dependent_variables: seed-paired change vs E001 in compute_only/fixed and joint/independent relative energy per successful task
controlled_variables: thermal target 80 C / hardware throttle 85 C
baseline: E001 (latest stored version) for HC1-HC3; fixed and independent within E001C for H1-H2
configuration: E001 design with calibrated overrides {'beta_compute': 0.983, 'beta_memory': 0.0}; every other parameter at its registry value.
evaluation_criteria: As E001 for H1-H2 (paired 95% t-CI, practical threshold 1%). HC1-HC3: for each scenario and seed, d = (a/b - 1) in E001C minus (a/b - 1) in E001 on E_per_success_kJ, with a/b = compute_only/fixed (HC1, HC2) or joint/independent (HC3); 95% t-CI over the 10 seeds.
known_limitations: Only clock sensitivity is calibrated. v_min_ratio, kappa_leak and p_leak_ref stay registry placeholders: their fits were rejected (docs/10). The measured power-vs-clock shape is not represented: with registry defaults the simulator misstates normalised power by up to 0.09 and energy per unit of work by up to 0.09 of the top-clock value. beta_memory = 0 comes from a pure streaming kernel and is a bound for LLM decode, not a measurement of it. One consumer GPU.
data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.

beta_memory.note: measured -0.05571 +/- 0.079 (95% CI) reaches the physical limit 0; transferred at the limit

v_min_ratio.reason: fit ended at the edge of its allowed range (v_min_ratio): the model does not describe these data

kappa_leak.reason: fit ended at the edge of its allowed range (c_W): the model does not describe these data

p_leak_ref.note: measured leak fraction 1.000 at 60 C scaled to the simulated accelerator
p_leak_ref.reason: derived from kappa_leak, which was rejected

inherits: E001 (same design, seeds and workloads; only the calibrated parameters differ)
disclosure: The calibration values were known when these hypotheses were written; E001C results were not. Acceptance rules R1-R3 were set after seeing the first desktop fit summary and before examining raw telemetry. Before registration, a forensic check re-ran 24 seed-0 E001 cells with the first (rejected) fit's values to identify orphaned time-series files; only their time series were compared, not their outcomes. No runs with the accepted values preceded registration.
